story_review.one_viewing_summary: The intended chain, reconstructed from the executable code: A generic drone's station opens on a caliche Permian pad and the drone lifts and flies out over the equipment while a Texas card pins the Permian and Austin. A flight screen lights and the companies' blue 'Anomaly' flag rises on a pump-pressure reading, tagged 'The companies say'. Under an 'Illustration of the method in EPA's letter' chip, an approval letter takes a September 30th, 2025 stamp and an Approved mark for periodic methane screening. The drone flies its plan to a white ring over a valve and an illustrative infrared view of the valve's shimmer opens. A seated inspector traces the shimmer with her stylus, presses a green confirmation with her finger and flicks a follow-up tag to the valve. The letter's protocol title highlights AI once. A separate, disclosed program is delayed to January 22nd, 2027 and proposed for rescission on October 7th. She presses her green mark again beside an empty AI box while the station closes outside.
story_review.opening_to_ending: It opens on a machine acting (the drone leaving its station) under the question of who decides that footage shows a leak. It ends on the person who performed the outline and confirmation re-pressing her green mark beside an empty AI box. The answer, a certified person, and the limit, the letter is silent on AI, are both pictured rather than only printed.
story_review.weakest_transition: s6 to s7 (38.72 s). The disclosed detour from the approval letter into the separate Super Emitter program is about 10.1 s of tags and calendar pages connected by news peg rather than cause. It is honest and labelled, but it is the least picture-led stretch before the close.

blocking_defects.failed_criterion: quality_contract.continuity ('explicitly introduces a sourced example; do not imply stock illustration is the actual case'). blocking_defects.defect: B's board treats s1 and s2 as the Chevron pilot (DroneLife c3, c4, c17) and switches to 'Illustration of EPA's method, generic inspector' at s3, through a source-example transition. But the renderer draws the same generic certified inspector in the pilot scenes. In s1 room-window, restingPerson turns her toward the window as the pilot drone's hood opens and it lifts off (registry room-window subject_ids include s1-inspector). In s2 room-monitor she watches the companies' alert on her tablet (s2-inspector). The person, room and window then continue unchanged into the EPA-method scenes, and the s9 window returns to the same pad. The s1 and s2 chip reads only 'Illustration. Generic drone and inspector'. The continuous person therefore cancels the s3 disclosure. The likely false inference is that Chevron's Permian pilot drones were already watched and confirmed by a certified inspector on site, under this approval. No source reports that: DroneLife describes monitoring and AI analytics from remote control centers, and EPA's letter describes review of collected footage under the approved method. Required correction: keep the EPA-method inspector out of the pilot scenes, for example by starting B's room story at s3. Alternatively, stage s1 and s2 with a visibly different, disclosed role and place, such as an operator at a remote control center as DroneLife describes, with a chip that says so. Do not return the review room's window to the pilot pad as if it were the same site, or disclose it as the illustrated method's generic pad.

blocking_defects.defect: In s7 room-calendar and s8 room-proposal, the same certified inspector sits at her desk reacting as the separate Super Emitter program's tag ('Leak reporting by certified third parties') takes 'Delayed' and then 'Will propose to rescind' (registry subject_ids s7-inspector and s8-inspector). The chip says 'Illustration. A separate program, no drone', which discloses the drone's absence but not that she is not part of that program. Putting the film's certified reviewer at the centre of a 'certified third parties' program that is delayed and to be rescinded invites the inference that the certified human check is what EPA is rescinding. That contradicts the closing answer and the narration's 'separate'. A avoids this because it has no person in s7 and s8. Required correction: either keep her out of s7 and s8, or extend the separate-program disclosure so it visibly covers the scene she is in.

story_review.one_viewing_summary: The intended chain, reconstructed from the executable code: In an inspection room a seated inspector turns to her window as a drone station's hood opens on the pad outside and the drone lifts off. On her tablet the companies' blue 'Anomaly' flag rises on a pump-pressure reading, tagged 'The companies say'. An approval letter slides onto her desk and takes its date and Approved stamps while she watches and taps a pen. On her wall monitor's live feed the drone flies to a valve ring and an infrared view opens. At the review screen she traces the shimmer, presses green and flicks a follow-up tag to the valve. She reads the protocol title, where AI is highlighted once, then the separate program's delay and proposed rescission. Finally she re-presses her green mark beside an empty AI box as the station closes outside her window.

Because that same person is also present in the pilot scenes and the separate-program scenes, the film implies she belongs to Chevron's pilot and to the program being rescinded. That blurs the limits the ending must keep clear.
